data_section_full_text:
2.1 SAMPLE CONSTRUCTION AND DATA COLLECTION PROCESS


The starting point of our sample is the list of S&P 500 companies
over the years 2003–2008. In section 4.1.2., we add three additional years

POLITICAL CONNECTIONS AND THE COST OF BANK LOANS 201

(2009–2011) to test the subsequent changes in firm risk following the
establishment of a political connection. For each of these companies,
we collect detailed loan data from Reuters Loan Pricing Corporation’s
Dealscan database and match this with firms’ accounting information from
the CRSP/Compustat database. The loan origination terms collected from
Dealscan are at the facility level, and they include loan size, loan maturity,
loan spread, loan type, and loan purpose. For each loan contract in the
sample, we collect the borrower’s political connection information directly
from EDGAR, which gathers information from the Securities and Exchange
Commission (SEC) filings of public firms. Following Goldman, Rocholl,
and So [2009], we define a company as politically connected if at least one
of the board members holds or held an important political or regulatory
position. <sup>8</sup> SEC rules require that public companies provide a proxy statement in its DEF 14A file containing a brief description of each board member’s career background. Based on this information, we are able to identify
whether each board member is politically connected. More specifically, we
search each borrower’s DEF 14A filing from EDGAR and then use a webcrawling program <sup>9</sup> to search for key words that can identify the director’s
title of political position. <sup>10</sup> Our study also utilizes finely defined and multidimensional information on private credit agreements in which covenants
are more detailed, comprehensive, and tightly set relative to other credit instruments (Dichev and Skinner [2002], Graham, Li, and Qiu [2008], Kim,

8 A firm is classified as politically connected if at least one board member and/or director either holds or held an important government or political position. Following Goldman,
Rocholl, and So [2009], these positions include: President, presidential candidate, member
of the House of Representatives, Senator, Cabinet secretary/deputy secretary/under secretary or assistant secretary, Governor, United Nations representative, Ambassador, Mayor, staff
member to the White House, presidential campaign or political party, appointed member of a
presidential committee or council, and Director/Deputy Director/Commissioner to a federal
department or agency (including CIA, FEMA, OMB, IRS, NRC, SSA, NRC, FDA, and SEC).

9 See Engelberg and Sankaraguruswamy [2007] for details about the SAS-based webcrawling program.

10 In order to make the searching process efficient and complete, we use two groups of key
words. The first group includes the titles of the political positions: president, presidential candidate, presidential election campaign, senator, house of representative, parliament, secretary
of state, deputy secretary, undersecretary, assistant secretary, deputy assistant secretary, chief
of staff, deputy director, regional director, managing director, associate director, chief officer,
deputy chief officer, executive chair, governor, commissioner, chairman, chair, chief counsel,
representative to the united nations, ambassador, mayor, white house staff, chairman of the
party caucus, chief acquisition officers council, director of administration, chief financial officer, national director. The second group includes the federal department and agency names
in case people work in those departments or agencies are left out: central intelligence agency,
federal emergency management agency, social security administration, civil rights commission, food and drug administration, security exchange commission, office of management
and budget, internal revenue service, reserve bank, office of thrift supervision, small business
administration, commodities future trading commission, office of the comptroller of the currency, national research council, and congressional budget office. In addition, to make sure
some of the federal agencies are still not being identified, we include “federal” as the key word.
